newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. senator warns aid to Palestinians may stop.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator warns aid to Palestinians may stop.

text.p: A United States senator said on Monday Congress would halt aid worth hundreds of millions of dollars unless Palestinians stepped up efforts to prevent attacks against Israelis.

Republican Senator Phil Gramm said Israel's "strong supporters" in Congress believed Palestinians were not meeting commitments to clamp down on militant opponents of their interim self-rule deal with Israel.

"Authorisation for Palestinian aid as you know expires on August 12th. It will not be renewed by the United State Congress in my opinion unless the Palestinians begin living up to the commitments they've made," Gramm told reporters before a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Two suicide bombers killed 13 people in an attack on a Jerusalem market on Wednesday. Israel has yet to publicly identify the bombers but Netanyahu has accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat of doing "damn all" to halt violence.
"I think we're very concerned about it. I think the peace process is jeopardised by it," Gramm said.

"Certainly the strong supporters of Israel in Congress are committed to the principle that Palestinian aid is contingent on their good word and their good deeds and we think they're very short of both right now."
Scheduled U.S. payments to the Palestinians total $500 million over the five years from 1994.

House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich said on Sunday some Palestinian leaders "have engaged in terrorist activities". He gave Israel his backing to take its own military action against militants.

Gingrich, one of America's most powerful politicians, said the United States should ..."flatly let it be known in the Middle East that we will be supportive of steps needed to protect innocent Israelis."
"The (Clinton) administration is very concerned about what happened and the growing sense of the administration is that the Palestinian Authority is not doing its job," he said.
